Lately, I find myself having feelings for a friend of mine and I know this person has feelings back. I've got so much guilt about it. We haven't slept together or anything but the desire is there. I should say that we would probably never work as a couple. I have tried telling my SO that I don't think we should be together and that I'm unhappy but my words go unheard. I don't have anyone to talk to IRL about this and I just wanted to hear what other people thought.

Consuming thoughts can take their toll. Are you the father, and your SO is the mother of the three kids? You just aren't married or what? Have some strength, you either need to put this other person out of your mind for good, or talk to your SO about what's going on. You'll regret any other option. If talking to your SO seems tough now, just wait until after you fool around, crash and burn. Why put yourself through that? You have a right to have feelings of attraction toward another like mind-ed individual. If you seem to ruminate, just remember, all parts of nature, have a breaking point beyond which things happen automatically. The more you can realize you are part of a larger dynamic, the less your motivations weigh in, but they do matter. It's tough when the discussion is limited to two people, because words themselves are already very black and white. Side, sides. Don't pick sides.

It sounds like you're unhappy and this other person represents some type of escape for you. Of course there is a strong allure to someone who promises relief from a pain you've been carrying for years. But this kind of escape is only temporary. And you're experiencing guilt because deep down you know this won't solve any of your problems. It will only temporarily help you feel better. But you'll feel a lot worse in the long run for betraying your commitments.

Get some counseling. If you haven't tried counseling yet, I don't think you're that serious about trying to save the relationship. If you're already past the point of wanting to work it out, then it's time to get your affairs in order and leave. Don't drag it out and make it a big sloppy fight. Don't let your desire for affection put you in a position to lose everything. If you get caught, you're relationship with your kids is going to be hurt badly. If you don't get caught, then you have to carry around a guilty secret for the rest of your life. Trust me on this. My grandmother came clean about her infidelity at the age of 74. She carried it around for 50 years and the shame of it made her bitter and judgmental for as long as I knew her.
